articles.title: Braided Hose Sleeve
articles.summary: Faint diagonal over-under strand weave, very low contrast, near-neutral shine with slight anisotropic stretch. A smooth slightly woven-looking sheen; the braid is too fine to pick out and just adds a dry metallic feel.
articles.what: Braided stainless and aramid sleeve strands in diagonal over-under rows. Up close: A very fine diagonal diamond lattice, about 12 px, made of faint crossing lines with tiny bright crossover dots, like stainless braid on a brake hose. Visible only as a delicate crosshatch in the lit band on metal. From a distance: A smooth slightly woven-looking sheen; the braid is too fine to pick out and just adds a dry metallic feel. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: trim, under stripes, bumpers.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Definitive Spec Replacements", or search for "Braided Hose Sleeve".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and roof on a metallic base
Spoiler and splitter for an aero-plumbing feel
No effect on numbers.
Almost invisible: a ghost diamond mesh in the brightest area
Pairs well with: matte, satin, metallic.
pitfalls: Not carbon twill: a thin wire-like diamond mesh, not wide flat tows
Not knurling: lines are woven, not cut diamonds
Avoid: large flat panels where the weave reads as noise, gloss base that drowns the low contrast.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.goal: Layer Braided Hose Sleeve over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Rubber Tire Cord
articles.summary: Satin black micro-ribs with faint worn streaks; low sheen, dry rubber feel. Disappears completely; the surface reads as the plain base finish, maybe a touch less smooth.
articles.what: Exposed tire cord ribs, rubber scuffs, and satin black worn streaks. Up close: Extremely faint, very fine diagonal crosshatch or tiny dot lattice, only a few pixels apart, visible as a slight screen-door fuzz inside the highlight on metal. On satin it is almost nothing. No ribs, scuffs or streaks show at 1:1. From a distance: Disappears completely; the surface reads as the plain base finish, maybe a touch less smooth. articles.title: Tar Snake Sealant

articles.what: Track tar-seal strips with glossy raised asphalt snakes. Up close: At 1:1 almost flat: a very fine, close-set grain of tiny zigzag ticks, only noticeable inside the highlight on metallic and as a dark wavy stitch in the floor reflection. No distinct raised snake strips can be seen in this crop. From a distance: Reads as plain satin or metal; nothing survives at distance. It changes the shine only, never the colour.
